For $0\leq m<k$ , one has $f_{m}=a_{m}$ . For $0\leq r\leq g$ ,

(2.8)

 $f_{k+r}=a_{k+r}+1-N2^{r}.$ 

Thus $N\leq M_{g,k}$ implies $f_{m}\geq 0$ for $m<L$ . Conversely, completeness implies $N\leq M_{g,k}$ .
